opening.headline: When you want to connect corporate document tools and AI and save repetitive instructions, you will learn what Gems and Workspace integrations do and how the permission scope of connected apps is determined.
body: If you're rewriting the format and tone instructions from scratch every time you ask for a draft report, and you're copying and pasting information from Gmail and Docs into the chat window, you're creating two inconveniences at the same time. This involves saving repeated instructions and safely connecting work data. Moreover, it feels unsettling how far AI can see.

In this lesson, we'll first look at how to create Gems that store repeated instructions and tips for writing good instructions. Next, we'll compare the Connected App feature that connects Gemini to Workspace apps like Gmail, Docs, and Drive, and the differences in terms for personal and work accounts. Finally, we explain what Gem does by writing reports in the same format every week.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.
objectives: Can explain the role of Gems and Workspace integration
The scope of permissions for connected apps can be divided according to account type and administrator settings.

items.prompt: Inconvenience 1: Writing the same instructions from the beginning every time
items.answer: Each time I am asked to draft a report, I rewrite the format, tone, and items to include. The longer the instruction, the easier it is to omit it, and if it is omitted, the format of the result will change.

items.prompt: Inconvenience 2: Moving and pasting work information into a chat window
items.answer: Copy the contents of an email from Gmail or a document from Docs and paste it into the conversation window. It takes effort to move it, and it may be out of sync with the latest content.

items.prompt: Anxiety: How far can AI see?
items.answer: Connecting the app means that AI will be able to view your mail and documents, so it is difficult to connect without knowing how much is allowed.
Repeat instructions are saved as Gems, work data is imported into the connection app, and the connection scope is confirmed by the account type and administrator settings.

screens.outro: First, let's think about how much AI can see.

screens.title: Think about it: What AI can see
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: If your company uses Gmail and Docs, how far should AI be able to see?
items.answer: Ideally, you should only see as much as you need for your work. The narrower the scope, such as a summary of a few recent emails or searching for documents in a specific folder, the better.

items.prompt: What is the range you can comfortably see and what range you should not be able to see?
items.answer: You can easily link publicly available meeting minutes, but documents containing personnel or customer information may need to be excluded from the scope of linking. It's not just the individual user that sets the scope, it's also the account type and the organization's policies.

items.prompt: Are there any instructions that you repeat?
items.answer: It is more efficient to write down conditions that are always the same, such as report format, email tone, and summary length, only once and save them. These instructions become the ingredients for Gem.

screens.outro: Let's start with Gems, which store repeat instructions.

screens.title: Gems: Saved Instructions
screens.lead: In the following steps, you'll find the order for creating gems and tips for writing good instructions. Select the next arrow to proceed.

visual.alt: Mockup showing the instructions field and preview window of the Gem creation screen.

steps.title: What is Gem?
steps.body: Gem is a custom helper I save to tailor Gemini's responses to my needs. You can create and write while logged in, and you must be 13 years or older to create a personal Google Account. Gems created in the Gemini web app also appear in the Gemini mobile app and in the Gemini side panel in Google Workspace.

steps.title: How to make
steps.body: Go to gemini.google.com on your computer, click Explore Gems on the left, and select New Gem. Name your Gem and write instructions to follow. You can preview your gem by entering the prompt on the right.

steps.title: All that remains is to save
steps.body: The gem will not be saved just by trying it in the preview window. After previewing, be sure to click Save. The most common mistake is that even if you wrote your name and instructions well, they disappear if you don't save them.

steps.title: Four Elements of Good Guidance
steps.body: Good Gem instructions consist of elements such as good prompts. The persona is the role the Gem will play and how it will respond, the task is what it will create or do, the context is about as much background as possible, and the format is about writing down the desired structure in detail. You don't have to use all four, but it's helpful to have a few.

steps.title: Help write instructions and add files
steps.body: If you're not sure how to write your instructions, you can ask Gemini to help you write them. Additionally, you can add context to the Gem by uploading a file, so it is easy to format it by uploading standard data such as a sample report. However, Gems cannot be used with Gemini Live.

screens.outro: Now that we've verified our saved instructions, let's look at connecting with Workspace.

screens.title: Workspace integration and connected apps
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn what connection apps are and how the conditions differ depending on the account type.

visual.alt: Comparison chart of conditions for using connected apps on personal and work accounts

Turn on Keep Activity (managed by administrator)

tabs.label: What is a connection app?
tabs.body: Connected Apps is a feature that allows Gemini to connect with other apps to process requests and provide more helpful responses. With your permission, it can even help you edit and manage the content of other apps. For example, summarize messages from Gmail, create calendars, and search for content across work apps.

tabs.label: Workspace app
tabs.body: Connect your Google Workspace apps to summarize, get quick answers, and search information from services like Gmail, Docs, and Drive. You can also request that you add, edit, and view tasks and reminders in Google Tasks, create notes and lists in Google Keep, and create and manage events in Google Calendar. If you want to disconnect, you can do so in Connected Apps settings.

tabs.label: Personal Account Terms
tabs.body: To connect to your personal account, you'll need to log in to the Gemini app, and it'll need to be the same account you use for Workspace. The Keep Activity setting must be turned on. If it is turned off, Connected Apps cannot be used on gemini.google.com. You can connect or disconnect which app you want to connect to at any time in the Connected Apps settings.

tabs.label: Work/School Account Terms and Conditions
tabs.body: Your work or school account must be an eligible Google Workspace edition and have the Keep Activity setting turned on. Only Workspace administrators can manage this setting. Additionally, your administrator must have turned on the ability to connect apps to Gemini. With a work account, no matter how much you want to connect, your connection will only go as far as your administrator settings allow.

tabs.label: Instructions for use and precautions
tabs.body: Select the app you want to use by entering @ in the input box, and specify the service or content type by writing keywords in the content instead of pasting the URL of the document or email. Gemini can give you hallucinations or out-of-date information, for example telling you the contents of old mail even though it is newer. So you have to click on the source listed after the response to check it.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the two features, let's apply them to our repetitive document creation tasks.

screens.title: Illustrative Example: What Gem Does for Repetitive Document Creation Tasks
screens.lead: The instructor explains what Gem and the Connect app do in the task of writing a weekly report in the same format every week. Select the next arrow to follow the steps.

steps.title: business reading
steps.body: The task is to write the team's weekly report in the same format each week. Now, whenever I am asked for a report, I write the format and tone from scratch, and copy and paste the content from last week's emails and documents. Change the structure to save repetitive instructions and connect and retrieve work data. In this structure, people have three jobs: setting guidelines, determining the scope of connections, and verifying results.

steps.title: Step 1: Format, word, and write down instructions
steps.body: Write down the format, tone, and items to include in the Gem's instructions. For example, the persona is 'the person in charge of organizing the team's weekly report', the task is 'summary of this week's progress', the context is 'the reader is the team leader, the length is one page', and the format is 'three headings: progress, issue, next plan'. You don't need to use all four elements, just a few can be helpful.

steps.title: Step 2: Upload sample report
steps.body: I'm uploading a report from last week to add context. Standards such as sentence length and level of expression are transmitted in the file, so any parts not included in the instructions can be filled in. However, we check before uploading that the sample does not contain personal information or information that should not be disclosed to the outside world.

steps.title: Step 3: Connect your Workspace if necessary
steps.body: If you need to pull up this week's content from Gmail and Docs, connect the Google Workspace app. Log in to Gemini with the same account and make sure Keep Activity is turned on. If it is a work account, first check whether the Workspace edition and administrator permission are required, and that Keep Activity is managed by the administrator. Unallowed ranges cannot be connected. When connecting, simply enter @ in the input window to select the service to use. If you make a request while not connected, a guide will appear asking whether you want to connect.

steps.title: Step 4: Check the preview and save
steps.body: Insert a prompt in the preview window to make sure your response appears in the format you intended. If you like it, click Save. Be sure to save it so you can use the same gem next week, either in the Gemini mobile app or in the Workspace side panel. If you just preview it and close it, it will disappear.

steps.title: Step 5: Check facts and connections
steps.body: When the report comes out, we check the facts ourselves. Responses written using hookup apps may be pulled from old mail or contain hallucinations, so check the source by clicking on the source below the response. Additionally, check the Connected Apps settings to see if the range of connected apps is as much as needed, and disconnect any unused connections.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Gem stores repeated instructions, and connected apps bring business data into conversations. When these two are combined, you get a personal assistant. However, the scope of the connection depends on the account type and administrator settings, and the user remains responsible for verifying the accuracy of the response.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the functions and responsibilities through examples, let us summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Summary: Guidelines and Connections Make Helpers
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Read it while thinking about the guidelines you want to create with Gem.

paragraphs: Gem reduces repetitive instructions with stored instructions. You have to give it a name and instructions and click Save to save it. If you just try it in the preview, it won't be left behind. The more specific the instructions are about persona, task, context, and format, the better. You can add context by uploading a file.

Workspace integration and connected apps bring work data such as Gmail, Docs, and Drive into the conversation. In addition to summary and search, you can also request Tasks, Keep, and Calendar actions.

The scope of permissions for connected apps depends on your account type and administrator settings. Personal accounts simply log in with the same account and turn on Keep Activity, but work accounts require an eligible Workspace edition and permission from the administrator, and activity settings are also set by the administrator.
Answers using connected apps may contain hallucinations or outdated information, so make it a habit to check sources.

To summarize, the procedure for creating a business assistant is simple. Write instructions, provide context with samples, link as much as necessary, save, and fact-check. By following this order, anxiety about how far the AI ​​can see can be replaced with confirmation of specific settings.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: Gems cannot be used with Gemini Live. Remember that the Gem's stored instructions do not apply when communicating verbally.

glossary.def: This is a helper that saves custom instructions that you use repeatedly. You must click Save to save it.
This feature allows Gemini to connect with other apps, write information, and even assist with operations with permission.
This is a connection that Gemini uses data from Google Workspace services such as Gmail, Docs, and Drive.
A work or school Google Account for which the administrator sets app connectivity and activity settings.
Settings to save Gemini activity. Connected Apps must be turned on to use them.

misconceptions.myth: When you use it in preview, the gem is automatically saved.
misconceptions.fact: Just using the preview window will not save it. You will need to give it a name and instructions and then click Save.

misconceptions.myth: I set up my work account just like my personal account.
misconceptions.fact: Work accounts must be eligible Workspace editions, and your administrator allows app connections and manages settings like Keep Activity. Even if users want to, they cannot connect outside of administrator settings.

misconceptions.myth: When you connect the app, the response is always accurate.
misconceptions.fact: Responses written through hookup apps may also contain hallucinations or outdated information. For example, if you have a more recent email, it may refer to the content of an older email, so you need to check the source.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Gem's are saved instructions and will not be saved until you press Save.
Workspace integration brings work data such as Gmail and Docs into conversations.
Linking of work accounts depends on your Workspace edition and administrator settings.
The app associated with the saved instructions creates a personal assistant, but it's up to the user to fact-check the responses.

options: It is not saved and does not remain
checks.explain: After entering the name and instructions, you must click Save to save it. Even if you try it in preview, it won't remain unless you save it.

checks.intro: When you create a Gem, check when saving occurs.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. You must click Save after specifying a name and instructions, and it will not be saved as a preview.

checks.q: Put the flow for creating a weekly report gem in the right order
items: Write down the format, tone, and items to include in the Gem instructions
Add context by uploading a sample report file.
Connect the Workspace app if necessary and check for administrator permission if it is a work account.
Check the response in the preview and save it with Save.
Check the facts of the results directly and check the scope of the connection
checks.explain: Create context with instructions and samples, verify connections, save, and check facts and scope of connections after use.
checks.intro: Arrange the flow of creating a weekly report gem in order.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. You've got the flow of instructions, samples, connection verification, storage, and post-use inspection.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. The context is created first, the connection is verified and then saved, and the fact-checking and connection scope checking are done after use.
